en.title: Champions Who Stay on Top Regardless of Other Rankings
en.description:
The champion gets n points, and the other places get n−1 down to 1 points. Count the participants who, after winning, have a total score at least equal to everyone else's no matter how the others are ranked. Ties for the top are allowed.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O and judging; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), and the second line contains n initial scores (0..100000).
en.explanation: Example 1: score 3 wins and gets 6, tying the 6 that score 4 gets in second place, which still counts as the top; score 4 also qualifies, 2 in total. Example 2: only 11 is within 1 of the maximum score, so the answer is 1. Example 3: both 10 and 9 qualify, so the answer is 2.
hints: Let the maximum initial score be M, and count the people whose initial score is ≥M−1.
